examples.en: The watcher kept an eye on the CCTV screens all night.

examples.ko: 그 남자는 감시자처럼 문 앞에 서서 우리를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The man stood at the door like a watcher and stared at us.

examples.ko: 감시자는 한 시간마다 건물을 한 바퀴씩 돌아요.
examples.en: The guard makes a round of the building every hour.

examples.ko: 게임 속 감시자의 눈을 피해서 앞으로 가야 해요.
examples.en: You have to avoid the watcher's eyes in the game and move forward.

examples.ko: 친구는 저를 자기 감시자라고 부르며 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend called me his watcher and laughed.
I walked quietly so the watcher wouldn't catch me.

explain: 지켜보면서 막거나 확인하는 사람이라서 긴장되고 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 시험이나 경기를 공식적으로 관리하는 사람은 '감독관'이라고 하고, 건물이나 장소를 지키는 사람은 '감시원'이라고도 해요. 소설, 영화, 뉴스에서 자주 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who watches in order to check or stop things, so it carries a tense, slightly negative feeling. A person who officially supervises an exam or game is a '감독관', and someone who guards a place may be called a '감시원'. You can meet it in novels, movies and the news.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어린 나이에 갑부가 됐어요.
examples.en: That person became a tycoon at a young age.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 갑부는 도서관에 책을 기증했어요.
examples.en: The richest person in our neighborhood donated books to the library.

examples.ko: 갑부라고 해서 모두가 행복한 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Not every super-rich person is happy.

examples.ko: 이 지역 갑부들이 모여 기부 행사를 열었어요.
examples.en: The wealthy people of this area gathered and held a donation event.

examples.ko: 그는 사업으로 큰돈을 벌어 전국 갑부 순위에 올랐어요.
examples.en: He made a fortune in business and got on the national rich list.

examples.ko: 갑부처럼 돈을 펑펑 쓰는 친구가 부러워요.
examples.en: I envy my friend who spends money like a millionaire.

explain: '부자'보다 훨씬 큰 부자를 말할 때 써요. 그냥 돈이 넉넉한 사람에게는 '부자'가 자연스러워요. '재벌'은 큰 기업을 가진 집안을 가리켜서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to someone far richer than a regular '부자'. For someone who is just comfortably well off, '부자' sounds more natural. '재벌' means a family that owns big companies, so it's a bit different.

examples.en: He is called a pioneer in this field.
The pioneers who moved west built a village.

examples.ko: 새로운 시장을 연 개척자를 만나 봤어요.
examples.en: I met a trailblazer who opened up a new market.

examples.ko: 우주 개척자가 되는 것이 제 어릴 적 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: Becoming a space pioneer was my childhood dream.
She is a trailblazer among women scientists.

examples.ko: 개척자 정신이 있어야 새로운 일을 시작할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need a pioneering spirit to start something new.

explain: '선구자'와 비슷하지만, 개척자는 땅이나 시장처럼 아무도 없던 곳을 직접 열었다는 느낌이 더 강해요. '~의 개척자', '개척자 정신'으로 자주 말해요. 사업, 학문, 땅을 열 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to 선구자, but 개척자 feels stronger about personally opening up a place nobody had been, like land or a market. It is common as '~의 개척자' and 개척자 정신. It works for business, scholarship, and land.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 한국 영화계의 거장으로 불려요.
examples.en: That director is called a master of Korean cinema.

examples.ko: 거장의 연주를 직접 들으려고 공연장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the concert hall to hear the maestro play in person.
They say Picasso is a master of modern art.

examples.ko: 이 소설가는 거장답게 문장이 아주 깊어요.
examples.en: This novelist writes very deeply, as a true master should.

examples.ko: 거장이 남긴 작품을 전시회에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the works the master left behind at the exhibition.

examples.ko: 젊은 음악가가 거장에게 직접 배울 기회를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The young musician got a chance to learn directly from a master.

explain: 한 분야에서 오랫동안 큰 업적을 남긴 사람을 높여 부르는 말이라, 영화·음악·미술·문학 같은 예술 분야에 많이 써요. 일상에서 어떤 일을 아주 잘하는 사람은 '고수', '달인'이라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a respectful word for someone who has achieved great things in a field over a long time, so it is mostly used for the arts such as film, music, art and literature. In daily life, people who are very good at something are also called '고수' or '달인'.

examples.en: The builder started construction on the new apartment complex.
My uncle works as a small contractor.

examples.ko: 건설업자 고를 때는 후기를 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: When choosing a contractor, be sure to check the reviews.

examples.ko: 집을 짓기 전에 건설업자와 계약서를 썼어요.
examples.en: Before building the house, we signed a contract with the contractor.

examples.ko: 그 건설업자는 약속한 날짜에 공사를 끝냈어요.
examples.en: That contractor finished the work on the promised date.

examples.ko: 믿을 만한 건설업자를 소개해 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you introduce me to a trustworthy contractor?

explain: 집이나 건물을 짓는 일을 하는 사람이나 사업자를 가리킬 때 써요. 회사를 말할 때는 '건설 회사', '시공업체'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person or business owner who builds houses or buildings. When talking about the company, people also say '건설 회사' or '시공업체'.

examples.en: My uncle is a financial professional with twenty years of experience.

examples.ko: 금융인들이 모여 새해 경제 전망을 이야기했어요.
examples.en: Financial professionals gathered and talked about the economic outlook for the new year.

examples.ko: 저는 금융인이 되고 싶어서 경제학을 공부해요.
examples.en: I study economics because I want to become a financial professional.

examples.ko: 그 금융인은 기부도 많이 하는 사람으로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That financier is known as someone who donates a lot too.
I think honesty is the most important thing for a financial professional.

examples.ko: 어머니는 유명한 금융인과 같은 회사에서 일했어요.
examples.en: My mother worked at the same company as a famous financier.

explain: 금융 분야에서 일하는 사람을 넓게 가리켜요. '은행원'은 은행 직원만 뜻하지만, '금융인'은 증권이나 보험 같은 분야에서 일하는 사람도 포함해요.
explain_en: It broadly refers to people working in the financial field. '은행원' means only bank employees, while '금융인' also includes people in areas like securities and insurance.

examples.en: That player is our team's rising star.

examples.ko: 신인 기대주로 불리던 가수가 상을 탔어요.
examples.en: The singer who was called a promising newcomer won an award.
Let me introduce this year's most promising talent.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어릴 때부터 수영 기대주였어요.
examples.en: That kid has been a swimming prospect since childhood.
The up-and-coming players are gathered and practicing hard.

examples.ko: 기대주 한 명이 마침내 첫 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: One of the promising young players finally scored his first goal.

explain: '유망주'와 비슷하게 앞으로 잘할 거라고 기대받는 사람에게 써요. 스포츠나 연예계의 신인 이야기에서 자주 들려요. '기대주'는 사람에게 쓰고 물건에는 '기대작'처럼 다른 말을 써요.
explain_en: Like '유망주', it is used for a person expected to do well in the future, and you often hear it about newcomers in sports or entertainment. '기대주' is for people; for works or products a different word such as '기대작' is used.

examples.ko: 저는 마흔에 대학에 들어간 늦깎이 학생이에요.
examples.en: I'm a late-starting student who entered college at forty.
That writer made a late debut.
Becoming a parent late in life, I'm more careful.
My father learned to drive late in life.
I started late, but I worked hard and caught up.
There are quite a few late-starting students in the class too.

explain: 보통보다 늦게 어떤 일을 시작하거나 성공한 사람에게 써요. 놀리는 말이 아니라 그래도 열심히 한다는 긍정적인 느낌이 있어요. '늦깎이 학생', '늦깎이 데뷔'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who starts or succeeds at something later than usual. It is not a tease and often carries a positive sense of working hard anyway. Common uses are '늦깎이 학생' and '늦깎이 데뷔'.

examples.en: My father signed the contract as my agent.

examples.ko: 바쁠 때는 대리인을 보낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: When you are busy, you can send a proxy.
A representative came and picked up the documents on my behalf.
A lawyer is the client's representative.
Try calling the agent directly.

examples.ko: 위임장이 있어야 대리인이 은행 일을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: An agent can handle bank business only with a letter of authorization.

explain: 다른 사람 대신 일을 처리하는 사람이에요. 은행, 부동산, 법률 일에서 자주 나오고 보통 '위임장'이 필요해요. 회사의 직급 '대리'와 소리가 비슷하지만 다른 단어예요. 가수·배우의 일을 맡은 사람은 '매니저'라고 많이 해요.
explain_en: A person who handles something on someone else's behalf. It comes up with banks, real estate, and legal matters, and usually a '위임장' (letter of authorization) is needed. It sounds like the job title '대리' (assistant manager) but is a different word. A person who handles a singer's or actor's business is commonly called a '매니저'.

examples.en: A new challenger takes on the champion.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에는 도전자가 백 명이나 나왔어요.
examples.en: A hundred challengers entered this competition.
The challenger kept running to the end without giving up.
He is the youngest challenger in this program.
I always work with a challenger's spirit.
Please give the challenger a round of applause.

explain: '도전자'는 대회에서는 챔피언에게 도전하는 사람을 말해요. 일상에서는 새로운 일에 용기를 내서 나서는 사람에게도 써요. 이미 이긴 사람, 곧 우승한 사람은 '챔피언'이나 '우승자'라고 해요.
explain_en: In a contest '도전자' is the person taking on the champion. In daily life it also fits someone bravely trying something new. The one who already won is the '챔피언' or '우승자'.

examples.ko: 우리는 오랜 동고동락 끝에 작은 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: After a long time of sharing hard times and good, we opened a small shop.
The bond from sharing joys and sorrows is not easily forgotten.

examples.ko: 그와의 동고동락이 제 인생의 큰 힘이었어요.
examples.en: The time I shared through thick and thin with him was a great strength in my life.

examples.ko: 삼 년간의 동고동락을 마치고 우리는 헤어졌어요.
examples.en: After three years of living through everything together, we parted ways.

examples.ko: 동고동락하는 사이라서 말 안 해도 서로 알아요.
examples.en: We share everything, so we understand each other without words.
The longer the time you've shared through good and bad, the deeper the affection.

explain: 오래 함께 지낸 가족, 동료, 팀처럼 정이 깊은 사이를 말할 때 어울려요. 짧게 만난 사이에는 잘 안 쓰고, '동고동락하다' 형태로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It fits close relationships built over a long time, such as family, coworkers or a team. It is not used for people you have only just met, and it is often said in the form '동고동락하다'.

examples.ko: 저는 십 년 동안 동료들과 동고동락했어요.
examples.en: I shared the ups and downs with my coworkers for ten years.
I met a friend after a long time who I went through army life with.
We lived through everything together like family, so our bond is very deep.
The coach built the team by sharing everything with the players.
It is an honor to share life's ups and downs with him.
I feel sad to part with the staff I went through so much with.

explain: 기쁜 일도 힘든 일도 같이 겪으며 지낸다는 느낌이라, 보통 '함께', '~와/과'와 같이 써요. 말할 때는 '같이 고생하면서 지냈다'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of going through both happy and hard times together, so it usually appears with '함께' or '~와/과'. In speech people may also say it in plain words like '같이 고생하면서 지냈다'.

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 모르는 게 없는 만물박사예요.
examples.en: My grandfather is a walking encyclopedia who knows everything.

examples.ko: 민수는 만물박사라서 뭐든지 물어보면 대답해 줘요.
examples.en: Minsu is a know-it-all, so he answers whatever you ask.

examples.ko: 저는 만물박사가 아니라서 그건 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: I'm not a walking encyclopedia, so I don't really know that.

examples.ko: 회사에서 만물박사로 통하는 김 대리에게 물어보세요.
examples.en: Ask Assistant Manager Kim, who is known as the office know-it-all.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터부터 요리까지 다 아는 만물박사를 만났어요.
examples.en: I met a walking encyclopedia who knows everything from computers to cooking.
Shall we ask our class's walking encyclopedia?

explain: 모르는 게 없는 사람을 조금 장난스럽게 칭찬할 때 써요. '척척박사'와 비슷하지만 만물박사는 아는 분야가 넓은 사람에게 더 어울려요. 말투에 따라 '네가 무슨 만물박사야?'처럼 비꼬는 느낌도 낼 수 있어요.
explain_en: People use it to playfully praise someone who seems to know everything. It is close to '척척박사', but 만물박사 fits someone who knows about many different fields. Depending on tone, '네가 무슨 만물박사야?' can also sound sarcastic.

examples.ko: 그 집안은 대대로 학자가 많이 나온 명문가예요.
examples.en: That family is a distinguished one that has produced many scholars for generations.

examples.ko: 명문가 출신이라고 해서 다 성공하는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Coming from a distinguished family doesn't mean everyone succeeds.
The heroine of the drama is the youngest daughter of a noble family.
They say two distinguished families grew close through a marriage.
They say that having grown up in a distinguished family, he has good manners.

examples.ko: 그분은 명문가를 이어 온 비결을 책으로 썼어요.
examples.en: He wrote a book on the secret to keeping a distinguished family going.

explain: 이름난 집안을 가리키는 말이에요. 학교는 '명문 대학'처럼 '명문'이라고 하고, 집안일 때 '명문가'를 써요. 역사 이야기나 드라마에서 오래된 좋은 집안을 말할 때 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a family with a distinguished name. For schools you say '명문 대학' (prestigious university) using just '명문', and for families you use '명문가'. It appears in history stories and dramas about old, respected families.

examples.en: He is famous as a master of the gayageum.

examples.ko: 명인이 만든 도자기는 값이 꽤 비싸요.
examples.en: Pottery made by a master is quite expensive.
I learned pottery directly from a master.
I went to see a Go master's match.
I hear the restaurant owner is a kimchi master.

examples.ko: 명인 소리를 듣기까지 삼십 년이 걸렸대요.
examples.en: They say it took thirty years to be called a master.

explain: '전문가'는 잘 아는 사람이고, 명인은 손기술이나 예술, 전통 분야에서 오랜 시간 쌓은 솜씨로 이름난 사람에게 써요. '장인'과 비슷하지만 명인은 공연, 바둑, 음식처럼 더 넓게 써요. 보통 '○○ 명인'처럼 분야 뒤에 붙여요.
explain_en: A 전문가 is someone who knows a field well, while a 명인 is a person renowned for skill built up over many years in crafts, arts, or traditional fields. It is close to 장인, but 명인 is used more widely, including performance, Go, and food. It usually follows the field, as in ○○ 명인.

examples.en: The dancer leapt high on the stage.
Being a dancer has been my dream since I was little.
That dancer was perfect even in facial expression.
The dancers practice in the studio until late at night.

examples.ko: 공연이 끝나자 무용수에게 큰 박수를 보냈어요.
examples.en: When the show ended, we gave the dancer a big round of applause.
Ballet dancers have distinctive feet.

explain: 무용수는 공연에서 춤추는 사람이고, 춤을 만드는 사람은 '안무가'라고 해요. 발레라면 여자는 '발레리나', 남자는 '발레리노'라고도 불러요. 앞에 '발레', '현대 무용'을 붙여 분야를 말해요.
explain_en: A 무용수 dances in performances, while the person who creates the dance is a 안무가 (choreographer). In ballet, women are also called 발레리나 and men 발레리노. Add 발레 or 현대 무용 before it to name the field.

examples.en: He is a gourmet who knows good restaurants well.
Many gourmets visit this restaurant.

examples.ko: 저는 미식가는 아니지만 맛있는 음식을 좋아해요.
examples.en: I'm not a gourmet, but I like delicious food.
I wanted to become a gourmet, so I learned cooking.
I prepared food to suit a gourmet's taste.

examples.ko: 친구는 미식가라서 식당을 고를 때 까다로워요.
examples.en: My friend is a gourmet, so he is picky choosing restaurants.

explain: 미식가는 음식 맛을 잘 알고 맛있는 것을 찾아다니는 사람이에요. '식도락가'는 먹는 즐거움을 더 강조하고, '먹보'는 많이 먹는 사람이에요. 칭찬으로 쓰지만 '입이 까다롭다'와 비슷하게 들릴 때도 있어요.
explain_en: A 미식가 knows food well and seeks out good meals. '식도락가' stresses the pleasure of eating, and '먹보' is a person who eats a lot. It is meant as praise, but it can sometimes sound like '입이 까다롭다' (picky).

examples.ko: 그는 이 회사의 발기인 중 한 명이에요.
examples.en: He is one of the promoters who set up this company.

examples.ko: 동호회를 만든 발기인들이 모여서 회의를 했어요.
examples.en: The people who started the club got together for a meeting.

examples.ko: 발기인으로 이름을 올리려면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I have to do to put my name down as a founding member?
At the founders' meeting, we decided on the name of the group.
I looked into how many founding members are needed.

examples.ko: 발기인에게 먼저 연락해 보는 게 어때요?
examples.en: Why don't you try contacting the founder first?

explain: 모임이나 회사, 단체를 만들자고 처음 제안하고 준비에 나선 사람이에요. 이미 만든 사람을 가리키는 '창립자'와 달리 설립을 제안하고 준비하는 단계의 사람을 말해요.
explain_en: This is a person who first proposes and prepares the founding of a club, company or organization. Unlike '창립자' (founder), it points to someone at the proposing and preparing stage.

examples.en: My dream is to become a ballerina.
The ballerina on stage danced gracefully.
My daughter has dreamed of being a ballerina since she was six.
A famous ballerina visited our school.
A ballerina turns standing on her toes.
After the show, we gave a bouquet to the ballerina.

explain: 여자 발레 무용수를 말하고, 남자 무용수는 '발레리노'라고 해요. 둘을 합쳐서는 '발레 무용수'나 '무용수'라고 해요. 영화나 노래에서 우아한 이미지로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means a female ballet dancer, and a male dancer is a 발레리노. Together they are called 발레 무용수 or 무용수. It often appears in films and songs as an elegant image.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 오랫동안 법조인으로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: My uncle has worked as a legal professional for a long time.
To become a legal professional, you have to study for a long time.

examples.ko: 법조인 중에는 사회 문제에 목소리를 내는 사람도 많아요.
examples.en: Many legal professionals speak up about social issues.
I have dreamed of becoming a legal professional since I was little.

examples.ko: 법조인의 말 한마디가 사람의 인생을 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: A single word from a legal professional can change a person's life.

examples.ko: 법조인 출신 정치인이 늘었다는 기사를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an article saying there are more politicians from legal backgrounds.

explain: 판사·검사·변호사를 함께 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 한 직업만 말할 때는 '변호사'처럼 각각 말하고, 여러 직업을 같이 가리킬 때 '법조인'을 써요. 이런 사람들이 일하는 사회를 '법조계'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a word that groups judges, prosecutors and lawyers together. When you mean just one job, you say it separately, like '변호사', and you use '법조인' when referring to several of them at once. The world they work in is called '법조계'.

examples.en: I left my child with the nanny and went to work.
My child's caregiver is very kind.
The caregiver reads storybooks to the children.

examples.ko: 어린이집 보모로 일한 지 삼 년 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three years since I started working as a day-care teacher.
It isn't easy to find a good nanny.
Let's say goodbye to the teacher before we go.

explain: 아이를 대신 돌봐 주는 사람을 말해요. 요즘은 '보육교사'나 '베이비시터'라는 말도 많이 써요. 어린이집에서 직접 부를 때는 보통 '선생님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It names a person who looks after children on behalf of parents. Words like '보육교사' (child-care teacher) and '베이비시터' (babysitter) are also used these days. When addressing someone at a day-care, people usually say '선생님'.

examples.en: In the movie, the sheriff protects the town.

examples.ko: 보안관은 가슴에 별 모양 배지를 달고 있어요.
examples.en: The sheriff wears a star-shaped badge on his chest.
I like the sheriffs in Western movies.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 새 보안관에게 도움을 청했어요.
examples.en: The townspeople asked the new sheriff for help.
The kids run around playing sheriff.

examples.ko: 그 소년은 보안관과 함께 도둑을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The boy caught the thief together with the sheriff.

explain: 보안관은 주로 서부 영화나 미국 이야기에서 들을 수 있는 말이에요. 한국에서 비슷한 일을 하는 사람은 '경찰관'이지만, 보안관은 한 지역을 지키는 이미지가 강해요.
explain_en: '보안관' is a word you mostly hear in Western movies or stories about the US. The closest Korean role is '경찰관', but '보안관' has a strong image of guarding one local area.

examples.ko: 국회의원 보좌관으로 일한 지 삼 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three years since I started working as a lawmaker's aide.
The president's adviser explained in front of reporters.

examples.ko: 새 보좌관은 일 처리가 아주 빨라요.
examples.en: The new aide gets work done very quickly.
The minister went into the meeting room with his aide.
My dream is to become an aide.
Please ask the aide about the schedule.

explain: 보좌관은 정치인이나 높은 자리에 있는 사람 옆에서 일을 돕는 사람이에요. 회사에서는 이 말을 거의 안 쓰고 '비서'라고 해요. 뉴스의 '국회의원 보좌관', '대통령 보좌관'에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: 보좌관 is a person who helps a politician or high official. In companies people say 비서 (secretary) instead. You will hear it mostly in the news, as in '국회의원 보좌관' (lawmaker's aide).

examples.en: The analyst looked through the market data.
I work as an analyst who studies data.
The soccer analyst explained the match in detail.

examples.ko: 분석가의 말에 따르면 내년에는 값이 오를 거예요.
examples.en: According to the analyst, prices will go up next year.
The company plans to hire a new analyst.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 나온 분석가가 이유를 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The analyst on the news explained the reason.

explain: '분석가'는 자료나 상황을 자세히 살펴서 결과를 설명하는 사람이에요. 뉴스에서 전문가가 나올 때 '경제 분석가', '축구 분석가'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여요. 연구하는 사람은 '연구원'이라고 해서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: 분석가 is a person who examines data or situations closely and explains the result. On the news you will hear the field in front, like 경제 분석가 or 축구 분석가. A person who does research is a 연구원, which is a little different.

examples.en: The cadets are marching on the field.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 공군 사관생도가 되려고 열심히 공부해요.
examples.en: My uncle studies hard to become an air force cadet.
Cadets live under strict rules.
At the graduation ceremony, the cadets saluted.

examples.ko: 형은 사관생도처럼 허리를 곧게 펴고 걸어요.
examples.en: My older brother walks with a straight back like a cadet.

examples.ko: 사관생도로 입학하려면 체력 시험도 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To enter as a cadet, you also have to take a fitness test.

explain: 장교가 되려고 사관학교에서 공부하고 훈련받는 학생이에요. 줄여서 '생도'라고도 하고, 학교는 '사관학교'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a student who studies and trains at a military academy to become an officer. It can be shortened to '생도', and the school is called '사관학교'.

examples.en: I went to an exhibition by a famous photographer.
I want to become a photographer.

examples.ko: 사진작가님이 사진을 아주 멋지게 찍어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The photographer took wonderful pictures for us.

examples.ko: 그 사진작가는 자연 풍경을 주로 찍어요.
examples.en: That photographer mainly shoots natural landscapes.
I went on an outdoor shoot with a photographer.
What should I do to become a photographer?

explain: 사진을 작품으로 찍는 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서, 전시회를 열거나 촬영을 맡는 전문가에게 잘 어울려요. 직접 높여 부를 때는 '사진작가님'이라고 해요. 간단히 '사진가'라고도 하고, 사진관에서 찍어 주는 분은 '사진사'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of someone who shoots photos as works, so it suits professionals who hold exhibitions or take commissioned shoots. To address one politely, say '사진작가님'. It can be shortened to '사진가', and a person who shoots at a photo studio is sometimes called '사진사'.

examples.en: He is the top pupil of a famous painter.
The master handed the shop down to his best pupil.
I learned so hard that I could be called the best pupil.

examples.ko: 우리 스승님의 수제자가 오늘 강연을 해요.
examples.en: Our teacher's best pupil is giving a lecture today.
It's not easy to be recognized as the best pupil.

examples.ko: 제가 무슨 수제자는 아니지만 열심히 배웠어요.
examples.en: I'm not exactly the best pupil, but I learned diligently.

explain: 스승 밑의 여러 제자 중에서 가장 뛰어난 제자를 말해요. 스승이 사랑하고 아끼는 제자를 말하는 '애제자'와는 달라서, '수제자'는 실력이 으뜸이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. 무술, 예술, 학문처럼 스승에게 배우는 분야에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the most outstanding pupil among a master's students. It differs from '애제자' (a beloved pupil), since '수제자' leans more toward being top in skill. It is often used in fields learned from a master, such as martial arts, the arts and scholarship.

examples.ko: 그는 모르는 사람에게도 스스럼없이 말을 걸어요.
examples.en: He talks freely even to people he doesn't know.
My senior came up to me without any hesitation and said hello.
We tell each other our worries openly.
The child took my hand without a bit of shyness.
If you need a favor, please feel free to ask.

examples.ko: 새로 온 동료가 스스럼없이 농담을 해서 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The new coworker joked around so easily that the mood got better.

explain: '말하다, 다가가다, 지내다, 묻다' 같은 동사와 자주 어울려요. 윗사람에게 '편하게 말씀하세요'라는 뜻으로 '스스럼없이 말씀하세요'라고도 해요. 가볍게 막 하는 것이 아니라 어색함이 없다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It often pairs with verbs like 말하다, 다가가다, 지내다 and 묻다. To someone older you can say '스스럼없이 말씀하세요' meaning 'feel free to tell me'. It means doing something without awkwardness, not doing it carelessly.

examples.en: That child was called a piano prodigy.
It was in the news that a prodigy had appeared.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 수학 신동이라는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I have been called a math prodigy.

examples.ko: 일곱 살에 대학 수업을 들은 신동을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met a prodigy who took college classes at the age of seven.
Prodigies often become ordinary as they grow up.
This movie is about a Go prodigy.

explain: '천재'는 나이와 상관없이 뛰어난 사람이고, '신동'은 어린아이일 때 이미 어른 같은 재능을 보이는 아이예요. 보통 '피아노 신동', '수학 신동'처럼 분야 이름을 앞에 붙여요. 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '천재' is an outstanding person at any age, while '신동' is a child who already shows adult-level talent. A field is usually put in front: '피아노 신동', '수학 신동'. It is not used for adults.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 노래를 정말 잘하는 실력파예요.
examples.en: This singer is a truly skilled performer who sings really well.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 실력파 신입 사원이 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A talented new employee joined our team.

examples.ko: 그 식당 주방장은 요리 실력파로 유명해요.
examples.en: The chef at that restaurant is famous as a real master of cooking.

examples.ko: 요즘은 실력파 밴드가 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: These days skilled bands are getting popular.

examples.ko: 실력파가 모인 대회라서 경기가 정말 재미있었어요.
examples.en: The match was really fun because it was a tournament full of skilled players.

examples.ko: 저는 얼굴보다 실력파 배우의 연기를 보러 가요.
examples.en: I go to see the acting of skilled actors rather than good looks.

explain: '실력파'는 겉모습이나 인기보다 실제 솜씨로 인정받는 사람에게 써요. 보통 가수, 배우, 선수, 요리사처럼 기술이 중요한 직업 앞에 붙여서 '실력파 가수', '실력파 신인'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 실력파 is used for people recognized for real skill rather than looks or popularity. It usually goes in front of jobs where skill matters, such as singers, actors, athletes, and chefs, as in 실력파 가수 and 실력파 신인.
